title: Feedback generation of quantum Fock states by discrete QND measures
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a control-theoretic problem in quantum physics: how to use feedback from quantum non-demolition (QND) measurements to drive a microwave cavity toward a desired photon-number (Fock) state. The authors focus on the mathematical design and proof of convergence for a closed-loop feedback scheme, rather than on human learning or educational intervention.

The proposed approach combines a discrete-time quantum filter, which estimates the cavity state from atom detector clicks, with a Lyapunov-based control law that injects coherent microwave pulses to increase the probability of a target Fock state. The system is modeled as a truncated finite-dimensional quantum Markov process representing atom-cavity interactions in a superconducting microwave cavity setup.

The paper proves almost sure convergence to the target Fock state under ideal measurement and model assumptions, and also shows robustness properties under certain detection imperfections through simulations. It further proves a contraction property for the associated quantum filter, suggesting that the estimator forgets its initial condition over time. The work is theoretical and physics-oriented, with no educational population, instructional setting, or teacher-coaching component.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a theoretical/control-systems paper about quantum feedback for photon-number states, not an education study. It does not evaluate any educational intervention, learner population, or instructional outcome.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no demonstrated educational impact relevant to teacher planning, coaching, or instructional feedback. The content is unrelated to the requested education/AI intervention topic.
